title: A native addon is refused cleanly, on purpose
intent: The only fixture that must NOT pass cleanly. Native addons cannot run in the browser lane, so the correct behaviour is a typed, immediate refusal. This proves the runtime can say no, which is what separates a limitation from a defect.
source: our own scenario, informed by the incumbent's documented --no-addons policy

steps.purpose: Install a package whose main path is a native addon

knownLimits: A PASS here would mean the runtime claimed to load a native addon and would be a false positive. A TIMEOUT or an unstructured crash is still a defect: refusal must be fast and typed.
